children: Bitcoin (BTC) traded within its tightest range since mid-September on Wednesday as volatility declined and analysts saw mixed signals beneath the surface.

The Bollinger Bands tightened, offering no clear indication of the next move, but renewed activity among longer-term holders and the return of spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) inflows suggested the market could be nearing a turning point.
Bitcoin’s Volatility Squeeze Leaves $81,900–$86,000 Range in Focus

Analyst Axel Adler Jr. said the squeeze itself pointed nowhere. "Narrow bands indicate market compression, but they do not reveal the direction or timing of the next move," he wrote in his morning brief.

Adler tracked the squeeze using “Bollinger Bands,” which measure how far price swings around its recent average. Bandwidth fell to 4.9% of the average price on Tuesday, from 11.6% a week earlier. Bitcoin also slipped to about $83,200 from $85,800 over that stretch, Adler Jr. said.
He put the top of the range at $86,000 and the bottom at $81,900. A hold above the top would signal an upward move, the analyst explained, while a hold below the bottom would point lower.

Adler's Volatility and Flow Index also showed a cooler market. It stood at 1,768, below its one-year average of 1,828. The index combined price swings, exchange flows, and the balance of market buys and sells.

Older Coins Tell A Different Story

A CryptoQuant analyst saw more activity underneath. Coins held for one to three years, and for more than three years, became more active in late September, the analyst said. That came as Bitcoin climbed from the mid-$70,000s to the mid-$80,000s. The analyst said similar spikes appeared in January and February, and again from late July to mid-August. "Movement doesn't necessarily mean selling or profit-taking," according to a CryptoQuant contributor.

What Drove Last Week's Dip

Glassnode’s latest weekly report showed who sold last week. Perpetual futures traders and ETF holders led the selling, according to Glassnode. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of about $681.1 million last week, according to SoSoValue data.
ETF buyers returned on Tuesday, however. The funds took in $175.62 million, their largest daily inflow since October 2, after $65.40 million in outflows on Monday.
Options traders bought protection. The 25-delta skew, which compares the cost of bets on a fall against bets on a rise, more than doubled to 4.46% from 2.1%. Other signs of new money held up too.
Glassnode said the monthly change in realized capitalization, a measure of capital held in Bitcoin, rose to 1.2% from 1.1%. More than 70% of supply remained in profit.
The squeeze followed a rebound led by spot buyers this week.
